title: One missing quote breaks the catalog
scenario: The delivery catalog contains three products, but its response requires every quote to succeed. Disconnecting only the lamp’s Shipping path rejects the complete catalog, hiding the healthy chair and desk too. Availability does not require Shipping and should still work.
why: This is error propagation through a coupled catalog response. A fast disconnect need not exhaust workers. An explicit unavailable lamp quote can preserve healthy products and stock information without inventing a delivery promise.
reproduce: Choose Shipping and click Disconnect in Network Faults. Compare “Refresh all availability” with “Preview all deliveries”. The complete delivery catalog should fail even though chair and desk have healthy Shipping paths.
ready: Start with “Clear all faults” and “Restore default settings” in Network Faults. Use the start launcher so fixed background traffic is running. In Storefront, compare the three-product catalog and its worker indicators. Keep the same traffic throughout, use fresh 60–90-second windows, and record changes in the cumulative rejected count rather than its lifetime total.
assignment: Can one unavailable lamp quote be contained to that quote instead of taking down the complete delivery catalog?

tasks.title: Compare both healthy catalog views
tasks.instruction: Refresh availability, then preview all deliveries. Record all three results, timings, queue state and an abort condition. Predict why Shipping affects one view but not the other.

tasks.title: Disconnect only lamp Shipping
tasks.instruction: Choose Shipping → Disconnect. Repeat both views. Record the failed whole-catalog response, the working availability view, and Shipping failures. Do not claim worker exhaustion if the queue stays empty.

tasks.title: Identify the coupling
tasks.instruction: Inspect “Customer request rate”, “Dependency outcomes” and worker indicators. Explain why one rejected quote prevents the aggregate catalog from returning its healthy products. Distinguish this from Challenge 1’s shared-capacity slowdown.

tasks.title: Allow an honest partial catalog
tasks.instruction: Reconnect Shipping first, then apply Challenge 2 settings in Fallbacks & timeouts. Shipping fallback and its 5-second circuit breaker are enabled; the timeout stays 3000 ms because disconnection fails immediately. Stock is still authoritative.

tasks.title: Repeat and measure the smaller impact
tasks.instruction: Disconnect Shipping again. Preview all deliveries: the catalog should return all three products, chair/desk with live quotes, and the lamp with an unavailable quote. Compare statuses, useful information and fallback activity. Clear all faults, restore default settings, wait for in-flight work and any 5-second cooldown, then verify all three products have live stock and delivery information. Submit your own measurements.

done: You compared both complete-catalog views before, during and after mitigation of the same outage.
You showed healthy chair/desk delivery information surviving while only the lamp quote remained unavailable.
You explained aggregate error propagation without assuming a fast failure saturates workers, then restored all paths and defaults.
solution: Without mitigation, a missing lamp quote rejects /api/catalog?preview=true. Availability still works because it does not call Shipping.

Shipping fallback converts the missing lamp quote into an explicit unavailable value. The complete delivery catalog returns useful live chair/desk information and lamp stock; it never invents a lamp delivery price or date.
The circuit breaker skips repeated lamp Shipping failures for 5 seconds and probes afterward. This outage primarily demonstrates error containment; queue pressure may stay low.
Reconnect, restore defaults and confirm live information for all products. Compare equivalent observation windows.

fields.label: Healthy baseline
fields.prompt: Record product and order-preview behavior before the outage. Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Hypothesis, blast radius, and abort condition
fields.prompt: Which customer functions do you expect to fail? When would you stop?

fields.label: Outage evidence
fields.prompt: Compare both routes and the Shipping dependency. Include statuses and a time window. Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: Should an unavailable quote block an informational preview? Explain your choice. Distinguish the roles of timeout, circuit breaker and fallback.

fields.label: Same-outage validation
fields.prompt: Record the route outcomes and fallback signal under the identical outage. Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Blast-radius conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did the blast radius shrink? What information remains unavailable? Confirm restoration.

overview.title: 2 · A missing quote hides the catalog
overview.description: Disconnect lamp Shipping, then shrink the impact from the complete delivery catalog to one unavailable quote.

mitigationHelp.description: Shipping fallback preserves the complete catalog with an explicit unavailable lamp quote. Its circuit breaker pauses failed lamp Shipping calls for 5 seconds; healthy product paths stay live.
mitigationHelp.instruction: Use Challenge 2 settings in Fallbacks & timeouts. Keep the default timeout for an immediate disconnect; a slow Shipping experiment needs an explicitly shorter timeout too.
